summary.headline: Emami Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR1,039 crores, but PAT fell 16% to INR137 crores on higher tax and input-cost pressure.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY to INR1,039 crores and domestic business grew 20% (12% like-to-like, 8% volume). EBITDA rose 6% to INR226 crores and PBT rose 4% to INR195 crores, while PAT fell 16% to INR137 crores due to a normalised effective tax rate. Gross margin moderated on input-cost inflation of about 360 bps (roughly 200 bps from the West Asia conflict and 160 bps from business mix). International business declined 12% because West Asia disruptions blocked OTC pain-management shipments from India. Management is moving disclosure from brand-wise to category-wise reporting.

financial_highlights.value: About 360 bps of gross margin pressure
financial_highlights.change: About 200 bps from West Asia conflict, 160 bps from mix
Includes about INR32 crores dividend from an international subsidiary, eliminated on consolidation

financial_highlights.value: Grew 61%; about 18% of domestic business; INR160 crores in quarter

segments.name: Hair and Scalp care
segments.commentary: Grew 11% in the quarter. Navratna Cool Oil grew strong double digits, Kesh King mid-single digits, and 7 Oils in One grew robustly.

segments.name: Skin care
segments.commentary: Grew 3%. Talc grew high single digits after a weak prior year; Male Grooming and BoroPlus grew low single digits.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Grew 2%. OTC grew high teens and Medico grew single digits. Management expects OTC double-digit growth for the rest of the year.

segments.name: Strategic investments (The Man Company, Brillare, Axiom Ayurveda, IncNut)
segments.commentary: Grew 61% like-to-like and is about 18% of domestic business. Management says the four start-ups are about EBITDA-neutral in aggregate and target INR750-800 crores revenue for FY27.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Declined 12% on West Asia disruption. Personal care is recovering from UAE, Germany and Thailand plants; OTC pain management is still blocked from moving out of India.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to more than offset the absolute increase in input costs during FY27 through further pricing actions.
Management expects the next few quarters to be better than Q1 on margins, with gross margin bouncing back as West Asia pressure eases.
Talc revenue is expected to return to FY25 levels, with substantially higher numbers in Q2 and a significantly higher full year.
International business is expected to show significant growth in Q3 and Q4 FY27 after a realignment of strategy.
Kesh King is expected to deliver double-digit growth by year-end. Strategic investments are targeted at 20-30% YoY growth, with high single-digit EBITDA margin at about the 3-year point.
Tax rate is guided to about 25-26% for FY27 as the company returns to normal taxation.
capex_capacity: About INR500 crores has been invested in Axiom, funded from internal surplus; some payments are still pending, so other income will be slightly lower than last year.
Three transformation initiatives (supply chain planning, Sales Code AI and an enterprise analytics hub) are expected to complete in FY27.
Personal care manufacturing runs from UAE, Germany and Thailand. OTC pain-management products are made only in India and are stuck pending ministry approvals to move abroad.
Management is looking to acquire more D2C businesses; Dhruv Aggarwal said two or three more acquisitions could be added.
demand_pricing: Management says the input cost inflation was among the most challenging for the sector in recent years, driven by crude oil and packaging costs.
Measured price increases were taken in Q1, and further pricing actions are planned; management says the mix shift toward lower-margin start-ups is hard to offset.
Organized channels grew 19% like-to-like; quick commerce is 35% of e-commerce business.
Brillare grew well above the average, helped by Rosemary oil shorts. Gross margin is above 70% for Brillare and IncNut and above 60% for TMC; none of the four start-ups is below 55% gross margin.
Talc was hit by a weak prior year and regional summer divergence in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the 61% like-to-like growth in strategic investments, and is it a base effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhruv Aggarwal said growth is broad across all four businesses, and that TMC grew well above 20%. He expects similar growth going forward and called it sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Why move to category reporting, and how does clubbing seasonal and non-seasonal brands help?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohan Goenka said the company has about 10-12 brands and new ones coming, so brand-wise reporting is no longer practical. He said Zandu Balm is classed under healthcare as it is primarily a healthcare product and not seasonal.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin hit is input cost versus structural mix change, and will it be fully offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Goenka said input costs rose about 360 bps, with about 200 bps from the conflict and 160 bps from mix. Pricing is expected to offset the input cost pressure, but mix is harder to offset, and he is not worried for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Will talc return to FY25 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Goenka said talc will recover to FY25 levels, with substantially higher numbers in Q2 and a significantly higher full year as FY26 was a low base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin of the strategic investment portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhruv Aggarwal said the four businesses are about EBITDA-neutral in aggregate. He expects high single-digit EBITDA margin at about the 3-year point and is targeting a healthy long-term profitability level.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR500 crore Axiom investment funded, and what is the other-income impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Sharma said it is funded entirely from internal surplus cash. Other income will be slightly lower than last year, as some payments are still to be made.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from crude and packaging inflation and the mix shift toward lower-margin start-ups. Management says margins will hold, but Q1 EBITDA margin was about 22%.
International business (down 12%): OTC pain-management shipments from India are still blocked; a resolution is expected 'in a few days' per management.
Kesh King growth slowed to mid-to-high single digits in Q1 versus a stronger H2 FY26; management expects double digits by year-end.
Strategic investment losses and whether the businesses reach the stated path to profitability; they are only about EBITDA-neutral.
Core business growth ex-start-ups and international is about 6% (domestic), below the headline; management expects better numbers ahead.
Tax rate normalising to 25-26% from the lower Q1 rate.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and on pricing and recovery in talc, international and Kesh King, but cautious on near-term margins and international, which management attributes to West Asia disruption. Several answers were qualitative and deferred detail, for example on start-up EBITDA margins and the timing of the international recovery.

Most likely, you will see a significant growth coming in from the third and the fourth quarter because we have got -- we have realigned our -- a lot of international business strategies have been realigned in the last 1, 2 quarters when all these disruptions were happening.
So overall, around 6% growth is there in the core business.

growth.why: Management guides to strategic investments revenue of INR750-800 crores in FY27, double-digit OTC and Kesh King growth, and a 25-26% tax rate, backed mainly by further pricing actions and start-up growth; no new capacity additions were quantified, and international recovery is contingent on regulatory approvals.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects gross margin to bounce back from Q1 as West Asia pressure eases and says pricing will more than offset the absolute input-cost increase, though the ~160 bps mix hit from start-ups is harder to offset; Q1 EBITDA margin was about 22%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or line was guided; the INR500 crore Axiom investment is an acquisition funded from internal surplus, and personal care already runs from UAE, Germany and Thailand plants.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic volume grew 8% like-to-like in Q1, with OTC guided to double-digit growth for the rest of FY27, Kesh King to double digits by year-end, and talc to substantially higher numbers in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it is looking to add two or three more D2C acquisitions, but no capex plan or utilisation level was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on talc, international and Kesh King recovery, but guidance is qualitative and the start-up EBITDA path is still undefined.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input-cost pressure from crude and packaging, the mix shift to start-ups (only about EBITDA-neutral), and blocked OTC pain-management exports could still hurt near-term numbers; the international business fell 12%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was named; management only mentioned new brands coming in general terms.

rows.label: OTC pain-management exports unblocked from India
rows.why: International business fell 12% because OTC pain-management shipments are stuck pending ministry approvals; management says a resolution is expected 'in a few days', and it expects significant international growth in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Strategic investments reach INR750-800 crores FY27 revenue
rows.why: The four start-ups grew 61% like-to-like and are about 18% of domestic business, with INR160 crores in Q1 and a stated FY27 target of INR750-800 crores, implying they must keep growing strongly through the rest of the year.

rows.label: Talc recovery to FY25 levels
rows.why: Talc grew high single digits in Q1 after a weak prior year; management expects substantially higher numbers in Q2 and a significantly higher full year as FY26 was a low base.
